title: Prime Minister  Shri Narendra Modi participates in golden jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Chennai, Tamil Nadu
subtitle:
The energy of our youth inspires great faith in India's future: PM

Today's youth aspires to be the strength driving the vision of a 'Viksit Bharat'; the innovative ideas and solutions needed for a Viksit Bharat, will shape the future of not just India, but the entire globe: PM

Given the infinite opportunities available in India today, I want every young person to see their future on that massive canvas; Because, this is your time, This is your opportunity: PM

I also recall the great saint Thiruvalluvar ji, whose teachings are crucial for all students; recently, I had the opportunity to present a Russian translation of the Tirukkural to Russian President Putin: PM

The Tirukkural is a wonderful guide for all those who wish to keep learning something new throughout their lives: PM

In one of his very famous Kurals, Thiruvalluvar ji teaches us that along with learning something, it is also necessary to adopt it in one's life: PM

While India prepares to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, we are also moving forward with the dream of hosting the 2036 Olympics: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 OCT 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the golden jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Highlighting the profound spiritual significance of the day, the Prime Minister expressed his immense joy at visiting the holy land of Shiva and Shakti on the very first day of Navratri. He stated that experiencing the positive energy, excitement, and vibrant enthusiasm of the youth while meeting the devotees of Mother Saraswati made for an incredibly auspicious start to the festival."I can see the future of India in the eyes of all of you,” noted Shri Modi.
Recognizing the immense potential of the younger generation, the Prime Minister emphasized that today's youth possess a strong desire to become the driving force behind the vision of a 'Viksit Bharat’.  He stated that the new ideas and solutions required to achieve this national goal will ultimately shape not only the country's destiny but the future of the entire globe."Today, the world is looking for solutions, and you have the potential to provide those solutions,” asserted Shri Modi.
Encouraging the students to dream on a massive scale, the Prime Minister urged every youth to envision their future upon the vast canvas of infinite opportunities currently emerging across the nation. He expressed absolute confidence that this collective national dream is entirely within their grasp during this era of unprecedented possibility."Together, We Will Do It!” affirmed Shri Modi.
Recounting a deeply personal anecdote, the Prime Minister revealed the interesting inspiration behind his visit, recalling a meeting with Girija Amma and several children in Nagercoil a few months prior."Her profound dedication, self-confidence, and unwavering devotion towards the future of the country left an unprecedented impression on my mind,” remarked Shri Modi.
Fulfilling the promise made during that initial meeting, the Prime Minister shared that Girija Amma's warm affection and his own deep respect for the historic institution compelled him to accept her invitation to the golden jubilee celebration. "I extend my heartiest congratulations to the Vishwa Hindu Vidya Kendra and the entire Hindu Vidyalaya family for this magnificent journey of Fifty Years,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Tracing the institution's highly inspiring trajectory, the Prime Minister noted that the Vishwa Hindu Vidya Kendra began as a very small school in Chennai's 'West Mambalam' in 1975 with merely seven students and limited resources. He praised the founders for relying on their strong willpower and an unbreakable spirit of service to overcome initial hardships and drive the institution forward despite lacking modern facilities or a permanent building."That is why, despite every difficulty, this institution kept moving forward,” observed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the massive expansion born from those humble beginnings, the Prime Minister celebrated how that small initial effort evolved into a massive educational movement over the decades. He noted the impressive scale of the institution's current reach across the state."Today you have 15 institutions in different parts of Tamil Nadu,” noted Shri Modi.
Honoring the foundational figures of the institution, the Prime Minister respectfully remembered the crucial contributions of Shri Jaigopal Garodia in constructing the school's building. He extended his deep gratitude to all the teachers, staff, parents, and alumni who dedicated their lives to making the Hindu Vidyalaya journey a resounding success."Fifty years of dedication, fifty years of commitment, fifty years of shaping young lives,” remarked Shri Modi.
Praising the institution for successfully blending academic education with strong patriotic values, the Prime Minister recalled mentioning Girija Amma in his 'Mann Ki Baat' program for brilliantly inspiring children to save just one rupee daily for the nation's soldiers. He commended the incredible collective impact of thousands of children joining this resolution to successfully raise forty lakh rupees."Indeed, what an inspiring example!” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing the profound power of incremental efforts, the Prime Minister stated that small contributions can generate a massive positive impact on society. He praised the Hindu Vidyalaya family for actively cultivating a great legacy of values, whether through supporting the needy during natural disasters or actively participating in cleanliness drives."Even a small effort can create a very big impact,” observed Shri Modi.
Invoking ancient wisdom, the Prime Minister paid homage to the great saint Thiruvalluvar, emphasizing that his teachings hold immense contemporary relevance for today's students. He proudly shared a recent diplomatic interaction where he presented a Russian translation of the Thirukkural to President Putin."His teachings are very important for all of you students,” noted Shri Modi.
Elaborating on the timeless guidance of the Thirukkural, the Prime Minister praised the text as a wonderful compass for lifelong learners. He highlighted a famous Kural by Thiruvalluvar that stresses the absolute necessity of actively applying learned knowledge to one's daily life, calling it a vital lesson for the students."Along with learning something, it is also essential to adopt it in one's life,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the deep cultural ties that bind the nation, the Prime Minister noted that the great poet Mahakavi Bharathiyar was profoundly influenced by the spiritual and national consciousness he experienced in Kashi. He encouraged the students to read and draw inspiration from the poet's expansive life and philosophy."The atmosphere of Kashi, filled with spiritual and national consciousness, had a deep impact on his thoughts,” observed Shri Modi.
Connecting his own parliamentary constituency to this shared heritage, the Prime Minister shared that the people of Kashi still fondly remember Mahakavi Bharathiyar today. He urged the youth to actively adopt the poet's famous mantra 'Achamillai, Achamillai' (Fearless, Fearless) to aggressively pursue their ideas and dreams."Dream big, think differently, and be fearless,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on his own life experiences, the Prime Minister explained that his deep understanding of the country was forged through extensive travel and learning directly from the people across different regions. He fondly recalled his participation in the Ekta Yatra from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in the early 1990s, where his enduring acquaintance with Girija Amma first began."Since then this acquaintance of ours has remained,” remarked Shri Modi.
Expressing his profound personal connection to the state, the Prime Minister stated that his extensive travels allowed him to intimately understand and appreciate the vast diversity of the nation. "The love that exists in my life for the Tamil language and Tamil culture has also been born from these very experiences,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Encouraging the students to actively engage in national integration, the Prime Minister urged the youth to travel widely and proudly carry Tamil culture wherever they go. He advised them to share Tamil poetry, stories, and traditions while actively forging friendships with people from vastly different backgrounds to strengthen the unity of the nation."The unity of our nation is built by the friendships you make,” asserted Shri Modi.
Detailing the unprecedented structural changes transforming the nation's academic landscape, the Prime Minister highlighted the massive expansion of opportunities available to the new generation. He provided stark statistical evidence, noting that the number of universities in the country has surged from 750 in 2014 to over 1,300 today, while colleges have increased from 38,000 to over 52,000, alongside the establishment of numerous new IITs, IIMs, IIITs, and AIIMS."The entire landscape of education in the country is changing today,” noted Shri Modi.
Underscoring the qualitative improvements driven by the new education policy, the Prime Minister celebrated the rapidly growing global recognition of domestic institutions. He pointed out that the number of Indian universities featured in the QS Rankings has dramatically increased from just 14 in 2015 to 52 in the latest rankings, directly resulting in vastly expanded choices for students."More institutions, more choices, and more opportunities for you,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Addressing the diverse aspirations of the youth, the Prime Minister acknowledged that many students wish to pursue non-traditional careers, particularly in sports. He assured them that the country is actively building new sports infrastructure and providing better training and support to ensure sports is treated as a viable profession rather than mere entertainment, which is already raising the nation's stature internationally."Young athletes are getting better training and support,” noted Shri Modi.
Outlining highly ambitious national sporting goals, the Prime Minister announced that the country is aggressively preparing to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and is advancing with the grand dream of hosting the 2036 Olympics. He declared that with the upcoming influx of massive global sporting events, the youth now possess the ultimate platform, the potential, and the full backing of the state."The opportunities are endless, and I am confident your generation will take India to new heights in the world of sports as well,” asserted Shri Modi.
Expressing his confidence in the younger generation, the Prime Minister stated that engaging with the students and feeling their vibrant dreams had significantly strengthened his belief in a glorious national future. He declared the youth to be the ultimate heroes who will shape and define the coming era."The future of India will be very glorious, and the biggest heroes of that future are you,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Reaffirming his absolute trust in their capabilities, the Prime Minister praised the immense talent, confidence, and capability of the students present. He invited the gathered youth to join him in making some massive, historic national resolutions."Today I want to reiterate some big resolutions with all of you,” remarked Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with a highly interactive and energetic pledge, the Prime Minister led the massive crowd in a resounding chant of "We will Do it!" to commit to a series of grand national goals. He urged the youth to fiercely dedicate themselves to building a Developed India by 2047, becoming a top-three global economy, establishing a self-reliant global manufacturing hub, hosting the Olympics, and placing an Indian on the moon.

title: English rendering of PM’s address during Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 OCT 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Arlekar ji, Dr. L. Murugan ji, Thiru Rajmohan ji, Thiru Nainar Nagendran ji, Dr. Girija Seshadri Amma ji, Thiru R. R. Gopal ji, my young friends, teachers and parents, my Tamil brothers and sisters, Vanakkam.
Friends,
Today is the first day of Navratri. To have the good fortune of coming to Tamil Nadu, the sacred land of Shiva and Shakti, and to have the opportunity to meet the devotees of Goddess Saraswati, makes this a truly wonderful beginning to Navratri for me. I can also see the enthusiasm of my young friends. I can feel this positive energy, this excitement. I can see the future of India in your eyes.
Before I begin, I would like to say that today I landed in Chennai ten minutes ahead of schedule. However, because of the way the programmes were arranged and some unavoidable delays, I was late in reaching you. I arrived later than expected, and this caused inconvenience to you all. For that, I sincerely seek your forgiveness.
Friends,
Today’s youth want to become the strength behind the vision of a developed India. The new ideas and new solutions needed for a developed India will determine not only India’s future but also the future of the world.
Today, the world is looking for solutions. And you have the potential to provide those solutions.
Friends,
Today, India offers infinite opportunities. I want every young person to see their future on that larger canvas. Because this is your time. This is your time. This is your opportunity. I am fully confident that we will fulfil this dream. Together, We Will Do It!
Together, We Will Do It!
Together, We Will Do It!
Together, We Will Do It!
Friends,
There is also an interesting inspiration behind my visit here today. A few months ago, our Girija Amma met me in Nagercoil along with some children. Their dedication, their self-confidence, and their devotion to the future of the country left an extraordinary impression on my mind. During that meeting, she invited me to this Golden Jubilee celebration. First, there was her affection; second, there was my own regard for this historic institution. At that very moment, I firmly decided that I would definitely attend this programme. On this occasion, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the Vishva Hindu Vidya Kendra and the entire Hindu Vidyalaya family for this remarkable journey of fifty years.
Friends,
Today, Vishva Hindu Vidya Kendra is celebrating its Golden Jubilee. This milestone is great, and its journey is equally inspiring. In 1975, this institution began as a small school in West Mambalam, Chennai. At that time, it had only seven students. Facilities like those available today did not exist. There was no permanent building. Resources were limited. But there was one thing: firm determination and an unwavering spirit of service. That is why, despite every challenge, this institution kept moving forward. Over time, this small effort grew into a major educational movement. Today, you have fifteen institutions across different parts of Tamil Nadu.
Friends,
On this occasion, I also respectfully remember the contribution of Shri Jaigopal Garodia ji. He made an important contribution towards the construction of the school building. Today, I also congratulate all the teachers, staff members, parents and alumni who have made the journey of Hindu Vidyalaya successful. Fifty years of dedication. Fifty years of commitment. Fifty years of shaping young lives.
Friends,
This institution is also an example of how an educational institution creates patriotic citizens along with providing education. I had also mentioned this in my Mann Ki Baat programme. Girija Amma gave the children a simple idea: each child should save just one rupee every day and dedicate it to the country's soldiers. When thousands of children joined this resolve, around forty lakh rupees were collected. Indeed, what an inspiring example!
Friends,
Small contributions can make a big difference. Even a small effort can create a very large impact. Whether it is supporting those in need during times of disaster or participating in cleanliness campaigns, these values form the great legacy of the Hindu Vidyalaya family.
Friends,
On this occasion, I would also like to remember the great saint Tiruvalluvar. His teachings are extremely important for all students. Recently, I had the opportunity to present a Russian translation of the Thirukkural to President Putin of Russia. The Thirukkural is an extraordinary guide for everyone who wishes to continue learning throughout life. In one of his famous kurals, Tiruvalluvar teaches us that it is not enough merely to learn something; it is equally important to apply it in our lives. And this is a great lesson for all of you students as well.
Friends,
You must all have read Mahakavi Bharatiyar extensively. The city of Kashi also played a very significant role in his life. The spiritual and national awakening that filled the atmosphere of Kashi had a deep influence on his thinking.
Friends,
I am a Member of Parliament from Kashi. Even today, the people of Kashi remember Mahakavi Bharatiyar. His words, “Achamillai, Achamillai” (Fearless, Fearless), inspire us to live without fear. Therefore, I would like to tell all the young people here: Give yourself a chance without fear. Work on your ideas. Dream big. Think differently. And be fearless.
Friends,
My understanding of India has been shaped by my travels across different parts of the country and by learning from the people I met there. In the early 1990s, I was also part of the Ekta Yatra from Kanyakumari to Kashmir. My first acquaintance with Girija Amma happened during that very journey. Since then, our association has continued.
Friends,
My travels gave me the opportunity to understand the diversity of India from close quarters. The love I have for the Tamil language and Tamil culture has also emerged from those very experiences.
Friends,
That is why I encourage you to discover India. Wherever you go, carry Tamil culture with you. Share Tamil poetry, stories and traditions with your friends. Make friends with people whose backgrounds may be different from your own. The unity of our nation is built by the friendships you make.
Friends,
Today’s new generation is receiving opportunities to fulfil its dreams that are truly unprecedented. Look at how the entire educational landscape of the country is changing today. In 2014, India had around 750 universities. Today, that number has grown to more than 1,300. The number of colleges has also increased from about 38,000 to more than 52,000. In recent years, the country has gained many new IITs, IIMs, IIITs, and AIIMS institutions.
Friends,
Today, the new education policy is improving the quality of education in the country. The global recognition of Indian institutions is also growing continuously. In the QS Rankings of 2015, India had only 14 universities. In the latest rankings, that number has increased to 52. The meaning of these figures is very clear. More institutions. More choices. And more opportunities for you.
Friends,
Every young person has different dreams and different talents. For example, many of you may wish to make sports your career. Therefore, the country is ensuring that sports do not remain limited only to entertainment. That is why new sports facilities are being created across India today. Young athletes are receiving better training and support. And India’s stature in the world of international sports is also rising.
Friends,
India is preparing to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games. We are also moving ahead with the dream of hosting the 2036 Olympics. In the coming years, when major global sporting events are held in India, our youth will have both the platform and the opportunity to showcase their abilities. Therefore, the youth of India now have the platform, the potential, and the support. It means the opportunities are endless! I am confident that your generation will take India to new heights in the world of sports as well.
Friends,
After coming among all of you today and feeling your dreams, my confidence has become even stronger. I can say with certainty that India’s future will be glorious. And the biggest heroes of that future are all of you. I have faith in your talent. I have faith in your confidence. I have faith in your capability. And therefore, today I would like to repeat some major resolutions together with all of you. After what I say, you must repeat: We Will Do It! Will you repeat it? Certainly?
Developed India by Twenty Forty Seven.
Developed India by Twenty Forty Seven. We Will Do It!
Say it with me: We Will Do It!
Developed India by Twenty Forty Seven, We Will Do It!
Top Three Economy, We Will Do It!
Self-Reliant India, We Will Do It!
Global Manufacturing Hub, We Will Do It!
Hosting the Olympics, We Will Do It!
An Indian on the Moon, We Will Do It!
Yes, We Will Do It! We Will Do It!
Developed Tamil Nadu, We Will Do It!
Developed Tamil Nadu, We Will Do It!
Developed India, We Will Do It!
Thank you so much.
Nandri, Vanakkam! (Thank You, Namastey!)

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates various development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore in Chennai, Tamil Nadu
subtitle:
It is a pleasure to be in Chennai with all of you, This is a historic day for Tamil Nadu; Today’s programme involves projects worth thirteen thousand crore rupees; We are inaugurating many completed projects and laying foundations for new ones: PM

India draws inspiration from its cultural strength, advances with scientific progress, and creates new opportunities through modern infrastructure. Our heritage and future aspirations are moving forward side by side: PM

In modern cities, we need holistic infrastructure;in the past decade, we have carried out a massive expansion of the metro network across the entire country: PM

Today, the port infrastructure across the country is also being bolstered so that the shipping sector can scale new heights: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 OCT 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone for, inaugurated, and dedicated to the nation several development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, today. Welcoming the esteemed dignitaries and the people of Tamil Nadu, he expressed immense joy at commencing his address in the vibrant state. Highlighting the historic significance of the day, the Prime Minister announced that the event involves massive projects worth thirteen thousand crore rupees. He explained that these completed and upcoming infrastructural developments will significantly ease daily commutes while simultaneously boosting industry and trade, generating vast employment opportunities for the state's youth. “I congratulate the people of the state on this occasion,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Acknowledging the spiritual sanctity of the day, the Prime Minister noted the commencement of the holy festival of Navratri and shared that he sought blessings at the Jalakandeswarar Temple prior to arriving. He praised Tamil Nadu as the sacred land of both Shiva and Shakti, sending festival greetings across the country from this pilgrimage site. “From the pilgrimage land of Tamil Nadu, I extend my heartfelt Navratri greetings to all countrymen,” remarked Shri Modi.
Paying tribute to the architects of the nation on their birth anniversaries, the Prime Minister recalled the immense contributions of Bharat Ratna Jayaprakash Narayan and Bharat Ratna Nanaji Deshmukh. He noted that their lifelong dedication serves as a profound inspiration to serve the country with heightened devotion. “From this stage, I bow to both these great personalities,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Sharing insights from his earlier engagements, the Prime Minister discussed his visit to the Brain Research Centre at IIT Madras, emphasizing that their pioneering research holds the potential to unlock numerous public health breakthroughs. He also expressed satisfaction over dedicating a brand new stretch of the Chennai Metro to the public. “Apart from this visit, I also had the opportunity to dedicate another stretch of the Chennai Metro to the public,” noted Shri Modi.
Drawing a parallel between spirituality and modern development, the Prime Minister observed that experiencing both the ancient temples and the modern metro perfectly captures the spirit of contemporary India. He stated that the nation is advancing rapidly by drawing inspiration from its cultural heritage while simultaneously building cutting-edge infrastructure. “Our heritage and our aspirations for the future are moving forward together,” asserted Shri Modi.
Reflecting on his expansive political journey, the Prime Minister marked the milestone of completing 25 continuous years as a Head of Government since taking his first oath as Chief Minister in October 2001. He explained that his quarter-century of service to the nation has deeply solidified his absolute faith in the democratic power of the people and the essential framework of cooperative federalism. “I have always moved forward with the mantra of developing the country through the development of the state,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Explaining how his tenure at the state level shaped his national vision, the Prime Minister noted that serving as a Chief Minister allowed him to understand state-level expectations. “Therefore, after becoming the Prime Minister, I not only tried to fulfill those aspirations but also tried to ensure that every state can achieve its aspirational goals,” noted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister remembered his fruitful dialogues with stalwarts like Karunanidhi and Jayalalithaa during his Chief Ministerial days, and his continued cooperative work as Prime Minister with leaders such as O. Panneerselvam, Edappadi K. Palaniswami, and M.K. Stalin. He emphasized that regardless of shifting governments, his commitment to Tamil Nadu's development remained resolute, and he now carries that same unwavering resolve while working alongside current Chief Minister Joseph Vijay. “Together with Chief Minister Joseph Vijay ji, we are taking this journey of Tamil Nadu's development forward,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Framing urbanization as a vital avenue for growth, the Prime Minister declared urban development in Tamil Nadu to be a supreme priority for the government. He expressed his firm belief that urban expansion should be viewed not as a challenge, but as a tremendous opportunity that must be supported by robust public transport. “If transportation is good, it increases the ease of living for the people,” asserted Shri Modi.
Elaborating on the necessity of comprehensive urban planning, the Prime Minister pointed out that merely widening roads is insufficient; modern cities demand a truly holistic infrastructural approach. He celebrated the massive nationwide expansion of the metro rail network over the past decade. “In 2014, the metro was limited to just five cities, whereas today, services are operated in twenty-five cities across the country,” noted Shri Modi.
Quantifying this rapid infrastructural leap, the Prime Minister highlighted that the national metro network has surged from approximately 250 kilometers in 2014 to over 1,100 kilometers today. He expressed great satisfaction that the latest expansion of the Chennai Metro will further enlarge this network. “This work has been done so that the journey of the common people living in Chennai becomes easier for everyone, and their travel can be completed in less time,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Pivoting to the critical role of domestic industry, the Prime Minister asserted that empowering states is the primary pathway to empowering the entire nation, which is precisely why the Central Government is aggressively promoting manufacturing in Tamil Nadu. He praised the state's vibrant small-scale industries and its workforce, noting that national campaigns like Make in India and Vocal for Local are delivering substantial regional benefits. “Every Indian is proud of the manufacturing sector of Tamil Nadu, the small-scale industries here, and every person working in them,” remarked Shri Modi.
Showcasing the dramatic success of the nation's industrial policies, the Prime Minister highlighted how strengthening the entire product chain, from components to finished technology, has transformed the country into the world's second-largest mobile manufacturer. He proudly listed the phenomenal growth metrics since 2014, including an eleven-fold increase in electronics exports. “Our defense exports have grown fifty times, and our engineering exports have also set a new record,” noted Shri Modi.
Connecting industrial expansion directly to youth empowerment, the Prime Minister stated that this massive manufacturing growth has successfully generated lakhs of direct and indirect jobs across the country, with Tamil Nadu making a highly commendable contribution. He announced the foundation laying for an advanced lubricant base oil project. "This will also create new employment here and will greatly help in reducing the country's imports,” asserted Shri Modi.
Explaining the symbiotic relationship between infrastructure and industry, the Prime Minister emphasized that a strong manufacturing sector fundamentally requires high-quality roads, railways, and ports to efficiently transport raw materials. “When such infrastructure is built, it also creates a lot of employment at different levels,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Detailing the economic chain reaction triggered by these developments, the Prime Minister noted that construction projects immediately employ engineers, technicians, and workers while simultaneously boosting small companies and factories producing cement, steel, and equipment. He explained that once completed, the enhanced connectivity from today's rail and road projects will prove critical for driving Tamil Nadu's industrial and service sectors forward. “Therefore, the rail and road projects whose foundation stones are being laid and which are being dedicated today are going to be very important for the progress of Tamil Nadu,” noted Shri Modi.
Focusing on the strategic modernization of maritime logistics, the Prime Minister announced that the nation's port infrastructure is being heavily bolstered to push the shipping sector to unprecedented heights, with Tamil Nadu playing a central role. He highlighted a recent landmark decision to invest approximately seventeen thousand crore rupees to transform Thoothukudi's VOC Port into a World-Class Mega Container and Green Energy Hub, capable of accommodating ultra-large container vessels. “This will help Tamil Nadu become a global hub for industry and transport,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting the operational successes of this maritime focus, the Prime Minister pointed out that both the speed and efficiency of Indian ports have drastically improved in recent years. He noted that significantly reducing ship turnaround times by half has allowed domestic products to reach global markets much faster than ever before. “Because of this, India's products as well are able to reach global markets faster than before,” observed Shri Modi.
Turning to the blue economy, the Prime Minister underscored the vital role of fishermen in the nation's Ocean Economy vision. He detailed that thousands of crores have been approved for Tamil Nadu through the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana and other schemes to upgrade fishing harbors, develop landing centers, and improve cold chain facilities. . “Help has also been provided to purchase transport vehicles to keep fish fresh,” noted Shri Modi.
Elaborating on the targeted support provided to coastal communities, the Prime Minister listed several key interventions, including the modernization of the Chennai Fishing Harbour and the development of a 'Sea-weed Park' in the state. “Through the Kisan Credit Card, working capital is now also easily available to fishermen,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address during the launch of development projects in Chennai
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 OCT 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Arlekar ji, Chief Minister Shri C. Joseph Vijay ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Shri L. Murugan ji, Shri Nainar Nagendran ji, my Tamil brothers and sisters, Vanakkam.
It is a pleasure to be in Chennai with all of you. This is a historic day for Tamil Nadu. Today’s programme involves projects worth thirteen thousand crore rupees. We are inaugurating many completed projects and laying foundations for new ones. Some will make daily travel easier. Others will strengthen industry and trade. Together, they will create jobs for young people across Tamil Nadu. I congratulate the people of the state on this occasion.
Today marks the beginning of the sacred festival of Navratri. On this auspicious occasion of Navratri, and in Tamil Nadu, the sacred land of both Shiva and Shakti, I also had the good fortune of receiving the blessings of Lord Shiva at the Jalakandeshwar Temple before coming to this programme. From this sacred land of pilgrimage in Tamil Nadu, I extend my heartfelt greetings for Navratri to all the people of the country.
Friends,
Today is also the birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Jayaprakash Narayan ji and Bharat Ratna Nanaji Deshmukh. The lives of both these great personalities inspire us to work with even greater dedication towards the service of the nation. From this stage, I pay my respects to both these great personalities.
Friends,
A short while ago, I had the opportunity to visit the Brain Research Centre at IIT Madras. The research taking place in this field can create many new opportunities in the area of public health. Apart from this visit, I also had the opportunity to dedicate another stretch of the Chennai Metro to the people.
Friends,
From temple to metro, these experiences of Tamil Nadu reflect the spirit of today's India. India draws inspiration from its cultural strength, advances through scientific progress, and creates new opportunities through modern infrastructure. Our heritage and our aspirations for the future are moving forward together.
Friends,
A few days ago, with your blessings and the love of the people of the country, I crossed an important milestone of twenty-five years as Head of the Government. In October 2001, I took oath as Chief Minister. Since then, the people of the country have given me the opportunity to serve first as Chief Minister and then as Prime Minister. During these twenty-five years, my faith in two strengths of democracy has continuously grown stronger. First - the people of the country. Second - cooperative federalism. I have always followed the mantra that the development of the nation comes through the development of the states.
Friends,
As Chief Minister, I personally understood the expectations of states. Therefore, after becoming Prime Minister, I not only tried to fulfil those aspirations, but also made every effort to ensure that every state could achieve its own aspirational goals.
Friends,
As Chief Minister, I had the opportunity to interact many times with Karunanidhi ji and Amma Jayalalithaa ji. And after becoming Prime Minister, I had the opportunity to work with Jayalalithaa ji, O. Panneerselvam ji, E. Palaniswami ji, and M. K. Stalin ji. Governments changed, but my commitment to the development of Tamil Nadu and service to its people always remained unwavering. And today, with that same commitment, we are moving this journey of Tamil Nadu’s development forward together with Chief Minister Joseph Vijay ji.
Friends,
Today, urban development is one of our major priorities in Tamil Nadu. I have always believed that urbanisation is not a challenge, but an opportunity. And public transport plays a very important role in this. When transportation is good, it improves people's ease of living. We all know that merely widening roads is not enough to create better transportation. In modern cities, we need holistic infrastructure. And therefore, over the past decade, we have undertaken a massive expansion of metro networks across the country. In 2014, metro services operated in only five cities of the country. Today, metro services operate in twenty-five cities across the nation. In 2014, India’s metro network was about 250 kilometres. Two hundred and fifty kilometres. Today, this network has crossed 1,100 kilometres. I am pleased that with this expansion of Chennai Metro, this network is growing even further. This work has been carried out so that ordinary citizens living in Chennai, working families, students, and senior citizens can all travel with greater ease and complete their journeys in less time.
Friends,
We have to strengthen India by empowering our states. Therefore, the central government is promoting manufacturing in states like Tamil Nadu. Every Indian takes pride in Tamil Nadu’s manufacturing sector, its small industries, and every individual working in them. Today, initiatives of the central government, whether Make in India or Vocal for Local, are also benefiting Tamil Nadu.
Friends,
Today, from components to technology and finished products, the central government is strengthening the entire product chain in every state. As a result of these efforts, today we are the world’s second-largest mobile manufacturer. Since 2014, our electronics exports have increased elevenfold. Our defence exports have increased fiftyfold. And our engineering exports have also set new records.
Friends,
Because of this growth in manufacturing, millions of direct and indirect jobs have been created for the youth of the country. And in this manufacturing growth of India, the people of Tamil Nadu have made a highly commendable contribution. Today, we are laying the foundation stone for an advanced lubricant base oil project. This will create new employment opportunities here and will also greatly help in reducing the country’s imports. To build a strong manufacturing sector, we need good roads. We need railways and ports for the transportation of raw materials. And when such infrastructure is built, it creates a large number of employment opportunities at different levels.
When construction takes place, engineers get work, technicians get work, workers get work, everyone gets employment. Employment opportunities are also created in factories connected with cement, steel, and equipment, as well as in smaller companies. And when a project is completed, improved connectivity helps industries and services move forward. That is why the rail and road projects being inaugurated and launched today are going to be extremely important for the progress of Tamil Nadu.
Today, port infrastructure is also being strengthened across the country so that the shipping sector can reach new heights. Tamil Nadu has a very important role in this as well. In this direction, the central government has recently taken a significant decision. With an investment of about seventeen thousand crore rupees, the VOC Port at Thoothukudi is being developed as a world-class mega container and green energy hub. Once this project is completed, even the world’s ultra-large container vessels will be able to dock here easily. This will help transform Tamil Nadu into a global hub for industry and transportation.
Over the past few years, both the speed and efficiency of Indian ports have improved. Because of increased speed, the turnaround time of ships at ports has been reduced by half. As a result, Indian products are now reaching global markets faster than before.
In our vision for the ocean economy, our fishermen play a very important role. Therefore, through the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana and several other schemes, projects worth thousands of crores of rupees have been approved for Tamil Nadu. Fishing harbours are being upgraded here. Fishing landing centres are being developed. Focus is being placed on cold chain facilities. Assistance is also being provided for purchasing transport vehicles to keep fish fresh.
Friends,
Whether it is modernising the Chennai Fishing Harbour for our fisherman brothers or developing the Seaweed Park in Tamil Nadu, the central government is supporting these efforts as well. Through the Kisan Credit Card scheme, fishermen are now also able to access working capital more easily. Today, fish production in the country has grown rapidly. Last year, our seafood exports reached their highest levels ever, both in quantity and value terms. This has improved the lives of our fishing families and people living in coastal communities.
Friends,
We want to build a Tamil Nadu that keeps reaching new heights. And for this, whatever support is needed from the Centre, we stand with you with full commitment. Let us together realise the resolve of a developed India through a developed Tamil Nadu. With this spirit, once again, I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all of you for these projects.
Nandri, Vanakkam!!! (Thank You, Namastey).

title: IITM Pune Hosts "The APARC Early Career Workshop" and Curtain-Raiser for ESTIC
date:

content:
The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) Pune hosted the Early Career Researcher (ECR) Workshop titled
"The ECR Nexus: Connecting Voices, Tools, and Science to Society"
today, at the Meghdoot Hall. The event served as a curtain-raiser for the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC).
The pivotal address was delivered by Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar, Hon'ble Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, who outlined the core vision and strategic objectives of the conclave. His opening remarks emphasized the critical convergence of science, technology, and policy in driving India's futuristic development and fostering a robust ecosystem for research and innovation.
The address underscored the Ministry's ongoing commitment to advancing critical scientific frontiers and creating collaborative platforms for researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders. By highlighting the primary goals of ESTIC, Dr. Srinivasa Kumar's address served as a call to action for stakeholders to leverage emerging technological breakthroughs toward sustainable national progress. The curtain-raiser has effectively built strong anticipation for the conclave, promising deep-dive discussions into transformative science and technology initiatives.
Key Highlights of the Event:
Opening Ceremony:
Featured
welcome address
by IITM Director Dr. Suryachandra A. Rao, Additional welcome addresses was delivered by Scientific Organizing Committee (SoC) representatives Dr. Ines Tritscher (Director of the APARC Office, Jullich, Germany), Dr. Jonathon S. Wright (Tsinghua University, Beijing) and Dr. Hindumathi Palanisamy (WCRP, WMO, Geneva, Switzerland), Vote of Thanks by Dr Suvarna Fadnavis (SoC & Project Director, CCCR, IITM).  ECR Workshop details were presented by session convener Dr. Aditi Modi.
Keynote & Expert Panels:
Dr. Maria Molina from the University of Maryland delivered a keynote presentation on AI and Machine Learning in Earth Sciences. An interactive panel discussion explored career trajectories within and beyond academia, featuring global experts from organizations such as NVIDIA, the World Climate Research Programme (WCRP/WMO), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, the University of Tokyo, and the Central University of Jammu.
Technical Sessions & Training:
Attendees participated in hands-on breakout brainstorming sessions focusing on key thematic priorities, a "Meet the Editors" interactive segment with representatives from Nature Portfolio and Springer Nature, and a comprehensive technical tutorial on the Earth System Model Evaluation Tool (ESMValTool) coordinated by Dr. Birgit Hassler.
Global Engagement:
The Young Earth System Scientists (YESS) community lead a presentation on international networking opportunities for early career researchers. The workshop aimed to foster collaboration, skill development, and cross-disciplinary dialogue among the next generation of atmospheric and Earth science researchers.
About ESTIC
The
Emerging Science, Technology, and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC)
is India's premier science, technology, and innovation platform. It brings together government ministries, policymakers, top scientists, academic institutions, industry leaders, and deep-tech startups to foster cross-sector collaboration and showcase cutting-edge research
and promotes innovative solutions to national challenges, driving India towards its goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.
ESTIC 2026 guided by the vision of “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.”  Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, this initiative brings together scientific minds, inspires young innovators, and strengthens India’s journey towards scientific excellence and technological advancement.
Designed to break down traditional silos between institutions and sectors, the multi-day conclave features high-level plenary talks, thematic technical sessions, and exhibitions focused on driving India's vision toward technological self-reliance and sustainable national progress.
About
APARC Early Career Researcher (ECR) Workshop 2026
The APARC Early Career Researcher (ECR) Workshop 2026, titled “The ECR Nexus: Connecting Voices, Tools, and Science to Society,” was organised on 11 October 2026 at IITM, Pune, ahead of the APARC General Assembly 2026. The workshop was designed specifically for students and Early Career Researchers, with the objective of providing a platform to discuss career development, emerging scientific tools, research challenges, scientific communication, and opportunities for greater engagement with the international atmospheric and climate research community.
Around
120 national and international participants
took part in the workshop, bringing together Early Career Researchers, senior scientists, experts, editors, and professionals from different scientific and institutional backgrounds.
The programme was structured to address both the scientific and professional challenges faced by researchers at the early stages of their careers. A panel discussion on career pathways examined opportunities within and beyond academia, while also creating space to discuss issues such as changing funding environments, mobility, access to research infrastructure and computing resources, international opportunities, and pathways to scientific leadership.
A central purpose of the workshop was to encourage open interaction between Early Career Researchers and established scientists while also allowing ECRs to exchange experiences with their peers. The panel and brainstorming sessions brought forward diverse perspectives on the changing landscape of scientific careers, including funding and mobility, unequal access to data and computing infrastructure, AI/ML, leadership opportunities, and the need to connect scientific research more effectively with society and policy. The Program was sponsored by the Minitry of Earth Sciences, WCRP, WMO, APARC, Foreschengszentrum Julich, Germany, IAMAS, ICMA, NASA, and private partners.

Keylong to house ICMR’s first dedicated centre for high-altitude medicine and public health research

New centre to strengthen climate-resilient healthcare, biomedical research and public health preparedness across India’s Himalayan region

date:

content:
The Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, will lay the foundation stone of the ICMR Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research (ICMR-CHAMP) at Keylong in Lahaul & Spiti district, Himachal Pradesh, on 12 October 2026. The Centre is being established by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) under the Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, to strengthen multidisciplinary research, innovation and capacity building focused on India’s high-altitude and climate-sensitive regions.
The Himalayan ecosystem presents distinctive public health challenges arising from high altitude, extreme climatic conditions, difficult terrain, geographical isolation and increasing climate variability. These factors influence disease patterns, healthcare access, occupational health and emergency response. The Centre will strengthen scientific evidence generation and the development of context-specific, scalable healthcare solutions for people living and working in these challenging environments.
The Centre’s research mandate will encompass high-altitude physiology and acclimatisation, mountain medicine, climate-sensitive and emerging diseases, infectious and non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, nutrition, mental health, environmental and occupational health, and disaster medicine. It will also explore the integration of digital health platforms, telemedicine, drone-enabled healthcare logistics and real-time public health surveillance to improve healthcare delivery in remote and hard-to-reach areas.
Located in Lahaul & Spiti, the Centre will provide an important institutional platform for sustained field research involving high-altitude and tribal populations in a strategically significant border region. Its location will facilitate longitudinal studies and investigations into the relationship between environmental conditions, climate variability and health outcomes. The Centre is expected to contribute to national priorities in tribal health, disaster preparedness, digital health innovation and the development of climate-resilient health systems, while strengthening India’s contribution to global research in high-altitude medicine.
The initiative will foster institutional collaborations with the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS), , research institutions of national importance in India and  the Government of Himachal Pradesh . These partnerships will support translational research, scientific exchange, capacity building and evidence-based policy development, advancing the Government of India’s vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat in health research and inclusive, climate-resilient healthcare.
The foundation stone laying ceremony will feature a traditional Bhumi Pujan, ceremonial groundbreaking and unveiling of the foundation stone, followed by the plantation of native Himalayan saplings under the Green ICMR Campus Initiative. The programme will also include the inauguration of a scientific exhibition, the launch of the Centre’s institutional video and website, presentation of the building layout, and the release of a commemorative postal special cover by the Union Health Minister.
The ceremony will be attended by Shri Sanjay Seth, Minister of State for Defence, Government of India; Shri Jai Ram Thakur, Leader of opposition, former Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh and Member of the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly; Ms. Kangana Ranaut, Member of Parliament from Mandi, Himachal Pradesh; Ms. Anuradha Rana, Member of the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly representing Lahaul & Spiti; andShri Ravi Thakur, former Member Legislative Assembly,.
Other distinguished dignitaries attending the event will include Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja, Director General, Armed Forces Medical Services; Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, ICMR; Smt. Manisha Saxena, Joint Secretary, Department of Health Research; Shri Vivek Kumar Daksh, Senior Deputy Director General (Administration), ICMR, Addl DG (Extramural) Dr Alka Sharma and Sr. FA, Dr Richa Pandey. Senior officials from the Central and Himachal Pradesh Governments, representatives of the Armed Forces, scientists, public health experts, research institutions and other key stakeholders will also participate in the ceremony.

Six-year plan to make India self-reliant in pulses by 2030-31
From Import Dependence to Self-Sufficiency
India is the
world's largest producer
of pulses, a globally important, protein-rich food crop. Pulses contain
20-25% protein
, more than double that of wheat and nearly three times that of rice. Pulses contribute significantly to India's agricultural exports and remain a vital part of Indian diets, ensuring
nutritional security
. Recognising this importance, the government launched the
'Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses'
on October 11, 2025. As the nation observes the first anniversary of the Mission’s launch on October 11, this landmark initiative continues its momentum, backed by a financial allocation of ₹11,440 crore spanning 2025–26 to 2030–31. The Mission seeks to achieve
self-sufficiency
in pulses production. It focuses on boosting domestic production, reducing import dependence, and enhancing farmers' income through a comprehensive value-chain approach.
A Mission with a Clear Target
Under the Mission, by 2030-31, production is expected to reach nearly
350 lakh tonnes
, with yield rising to
1,130 kg per hectare
. Key strategic measures driving these targets include
:
Focus on enhancing production of
Tur, Urad and Masoor
Promotion of
climate-resilient seeds
and improved seed quality
Distribution of
87.5 lakh free seed kits and 126 lakh quintals of certified seeds
over six years
Expands pulse cultivation area by 35 lakh hectares to reach a total targeted area of 310 lakh hectares by 2030–31.
Cluster-based approach
covering
489 districts
to intensify production
Establishment of
1,000 processing units
(dal mills)
Assured procurement
of Tur, Urad and Masoor via
NCCF and NAFED from willing and registered farmer.
Expected to
reduce import dependence
and
conserve foreign exchange
India’s Pulse Powerhouse
India’s pulse sector showed strong growth in domestic production, farming area, and crop yield during 2025-26. Steady agricultural progress and strong local output continue to strengthen the nation’s pulse economy.
India’s total pulse production rose to
274.09 lakh tonnes
in 2025-26
(
3rd Advance Estimates
)
from
256.83 lakh tonnes
in 2024-25.
India's pulse cultivation area expanded significantly from
277.20 lakh hectares in 2024-25
to
286.46 lakh hectares in 2025-26
.
The major regions of
Pulse cultivation
are Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.
National pulse productivity improved as the overall yield increased from
926 kg per hectare in 2024-25
to
957 kg per hectare in 2025-26
.
India’s pulses imports declined by
31.52%
, from
₹
46,427.60 crore in 2024
-

to
₹
31,793.59 crore in 2025
-
26
.
India’s pulses exports rose
13.40%
, from
USD 855 million in 2024-25
to
USD 969.53 million in 2025-26
. The total export volume reached a total volume of
10.01 lakh tonnes
during 2025–26.
In 2025-26, major export destinations included
China, UAE, Bangladesh, the U.S.A., and Sri Lanka
.
Rising MSP, Assured Procurement
The government continues to strengthen price security for pulse farmers through substantial increases in Minimum Support Prices. Higher support prices ensure fair returns and incentivize increased domestic production of key pulse crops.
For the marketing season
2024-25
, the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for
Urad
was fixed at
₹
7,400
per quintal, which was increased by
₹
800
(
10.81%

₹
8,200
per quintal for
2026-27

For the year
2024-25
, the MSP for
Tur
(
Arhar

₹
7,550
per quintal, which saw an enhancement of
₹
900
(
11.92%
) to reach
₹
8,450
per quintal in
2026-27

Under the Mission, National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF) and National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Limited (NAFED) are authorized to procure 100% of Tur, Masur, and Urad for a period of four years (2025–26 to 2028–29). NCCF achieved a total pulses procurement of
10.55 lakh tonnes
across 9 states. A total Minimum Support Price (MSP) value of

Mission’s Key Early Progress
The Mission's early progress reflects steady momentum in building infrastructure and expanding farmer support. Key achievements so far include:
The Mission
envisages 1,000 pulse processing units
, with
528 units already allocated
to States and Union Territories in the
first phase
.
A total of
23 pulse processing
units have been approved for Creation and Expansion of Food Processing and Preservation Capacities (CEFPPC) under Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY
)

18 pulse processing units
have been successfully completed.
To
boost pulses in rice-fallow areas
, the Mission targets to distribute
87.5 lakh seed kits
over six years, with
9.25 lakh kits distributed
during Rabi 2025-26.
Digital Monitoring & Seed Traceability
The government leverages advanced digital platforms to ensure seamless monitoring, real-time oversight, and targeted execution across all levels:
A
three-tier Steering Committee network
monitors planning, implementation, and progress at the national, state, and district levels.
The
Krishi Mapper application
enables precise geo-fencing, land geo-tagging, and real-time tracking of seed variety demonstrations and yields.
Seed Authentication, Traceability & Holistic Inventory (
SATHI)
portal provides a holistic approach to encompass the seed life cycle over seed generations. This measure is achieved through automation of the seed supply chain, starting from seed production to certification and seed sale.
AgriStack & Digital Crop Survey
: Integrates unified Farmer IDs with Soil Health Card analytics and verified plot surveys to ensure targeted nutrient delivery and accurate harvest forecasts.
Verification platforms like
E-Samriddhi and Vistaar
ensure direct payments, real-time market data, and domestic price stability.
Sowing Today, Securing Tomorrow
The early momentum indicates that the
Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses
is successfully bridging policy intent and ground-level execution. Guaranteed price support has restored grower confidence, while digital platforms like SATHI and e-Samriddhi ensure full supply chain transparency. As India moves toward its
2030–31 production target of 350 lakh tonnes
, this integrated value-chain framework promises not only long-term national protein security and foreign exchange savings, but also a replicable model for self-sufficiency across the broader agricultural economy.
